solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Snare Pop's heart in bouquet

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, as a thing placed in a holder

parts.note: first part of NOSE, the bouquet or aroma of a wine

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, so only the middle of the short word is kept

parts.note: the middle letter of POP
rest of NOSE, wrapped around the middle letter

explanation.surface: A trapper catches someone's dad by the flowers he is holding.
explanation.walkthrough: NOSE, a wine's bouquet, takes the O from the middle of POP: NO(O)SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a running loop of rope, the commonest kind of snare for catching animals.

clue.text: Snooping round that girl's greasy spoon?

indicators.note: round means encircling, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: nosy means prying
her is the possessive for that girl

explanation.surface: A busybody pries around some woman's café.
explanation.walkthrough: A greasy spoon is a cheap British café serving fried food.
explanation.definitionFit: A noshery is a slang word for an eating place, and a greasy spoon is a cheap café.

clue.text: Happily our pie packs figurative food for thought for addict?

indicators.note: happily can mean by chance or haphazardly, so the letters fall out in a new order
to pack is to stuff something inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: the six letters rearranged
meat in the figurative sense of substance, matter to chew on

explanation.surface: A cheerful pie stuffed with meat feeds a hungry thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: De Quincey's Confessions of an English Opium-Eater made the term famous.
explanation.definitionFit: An opium eater is one who habitually takes opium, a drug addict in old parlance.

clue.text: Witness arrival of moral shortcoming about English eccentricity

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece encircles the others

parts.note: a sin is a moral failing
E is the abbreviation for English
e is the mathematical symbol for the eccentricity of a conic

explanation.surface: Someone notices an Englishman's odd vice turning up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentricity' looks like an oddity, but it is the maths term whose symbol is lower-case e.
explanation.definitionFit: To see in the New Year is to stay up to witness its arrival, so the phrase means watch something come in.

clue.text: Grass's especially cunning conduct close to mafioso

parts.note: ESP is the abbreviation for especially
art is cunning or craft in behaviour

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the last letter is used

parts.note: last letter of mafioso

explanation.surface: An informer's crafty behaviour suits the end of a gangster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass's' looks like an informer, but the definition is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Esparto is a tough Spanish grass used to make rope, paper and mats.

clue.text: Paladins must protect power and soft pelts

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround it, so one group of letters encloses the others

parts.note: the paladins were Charlemagne's twelve peers
P is the physics symbol for power
p, piano, is the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: Knights in armour stand guard over a ruler while being hit by missiles.
explanation.walkthrough: PEERS holds the two Ps: PE(PP)ERS. 'Pelts' is a verb here, not animal skins.
explanation.definitionFit: To pepper is to bombard with shot or missiles, the same action as pelting.

clue.text: Trot on the spot is socially crass (not new) in cock-up

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
not new says the abbreviation for new is taken away

parts.note: first part of PIE, a printer's jumble of type, a mess
NAFF, British slang for tacky, without the N
end of PIE, closing around the middle

explanation.surface: Jogging in place is uncool and something of a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: Naff is British slang for tasteless; pie is type that has been knocked into a muddle. AFF goes inside PIE.
explanation.definitionFit: The piaffe is a dressage movement in which the horse trots without moving forward.

clue.text: European matches lifted honour

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifted means raised from the bottom, so the word runs upwards

parts.note: meets are sporting matches

explanation.surface: A continental side's fixtures raised its standing.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem someone is to hold them in high regard, the same as to honour them.

clue.text: God, one's an old heathen

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
I'M, one is, with I as one

explanation.surface: A deity is declared to be a pagan.
explanation.walkthrough: PAN + I'M. Panim is a Spenserian form of paynim.
explanation.definitionFit: Panim is an archaic spelling of paynim, a pagan or non-Christian, so an old word for a heathen.

clue.text: Backs of American wagons need altering to hold iron and steel initially

indicators.note: altering means changing, so the letters are rearranged
to hold something is to keep it inside

parts.note: the four letters rearranged
iron and gat are both slang for a gun

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: first letter of steel

explanation.surface: American wagons need refitting with metal fixtures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron' looks like the metal, but it is gangster slang for a gun, as is GAT. GAT goes inside the rearranged NEED, then S.
explanation.definitionFit: An endgate is the hinged tailboard at the back of a wagon or truck, chiefly an American term.

clue.text: Appreciate old domestic servants turning up

indicators.note: turning up in a down entry means running from the bottom upwards, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: esnes were Old English labourers or slaves

explanation.surface: An employer values former household staff when they arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: To sense something is to perceive or understand it, a meaning of appreciate.

clue.text: Manoeuvring in secret as those led by Michelle Dubois?

indicators.note: manoeuvring means moving things about into new positions, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the three words supply all ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Undercover operators move about in secret, like Michelle's band in the wartime sitcom.
explanation.walkthrough: Michelle Dubois led the French Resistance cell in the British TV sitcom 'Allo 'Allo!, which famously operated in secret, so the wordplay also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In 'Allo 'Allo! Michelle of the Resistance commanded the underground fighters, so her followers are the Resistance.

clue.text: Byway is going around area shrouded in obscurity

indicators.note: going around means turning to face the other way, so the short word is read back to front

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something shrouded is wrapped up inside a covering, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: depth can mean obscurity, as in a meaning too deep to grasp
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A minor road winds round a district lost in gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: Depth in the sense of profundity beyond understanding is a recognised dictionary meaning of obscurity.
explanation.definitionFit: A side path is a minor track off a main route, which is just what a byway is.

clue.text: Gooseberry plant bound by gardener finally

parts.note: to plant a body is to inter it
to lope is to run with long bounding strides

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word

parts.note: last letter of gardener

explanation.surface: A gardener's bush is set and staked in the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gooseberry' and 'plant' both look horticultural; in Britain, playing gooseberry is being the unwanted third person with a couple.
explanation.definitionFit: A gooseberry is an unwanted third party intruding on a couple, so an interloper.

clue.text: Shed with cigar in every second place for Cuban beast

parts.note: a shed is a hut

indicators.note: taking only what sits in each even position skips alternate letters of the word

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of cigar

explanation.surface: Someone smokes a Havana in a garden shed, as Cubans might.
explanation.definitionFit: The hutia is a large rodent native to Cuba and other Caribbean islands, so a Cuban animal.

clue.text: Fault is accepting good old promises

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so a letter is placed inside the word

parts.note: a sin is a moral fault
G is the abbreviation for good
the contracted form 's

explanation.surface: A wrongdoing is excused by taking past pledges on trust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' supplies only its contracted 's, as in 'it's'.
explanation.definitionFit: In older usage to sign was to pledge or betoken, so signs could stand for promises or tokens.

clue.text: Shriek — special jug especially for Americans!

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for special
creamer is chiefly North American for a cream jug

explanation.surface: Someone screams at a special jug, as Americans tend to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shriek' is printers' slang for an exclamation mark, and so is screamer, which the closing '!' illustrates.
explanation.definitionFit: Both shriek and screamer are slang names for the exclamation mark among printers and journalists.

clue.text: With zebra held back pal pauses

indicators.note: held back suggests pulled the other way, so the word runs from right to left

parts.note: a zebra is slang for a referee, from the striped shirt
a mate is a pal

explanation.surface: A friend waits while a striped animal is restrained.
explanation.walkthrough: In American football referees wear black-and-white stripes, hence 'zebra'; REF reversed gives FER, then MATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fermate is the plural of fermata, the musical pause sign that holds a note beyond its value.

clue.text: Give details of townie mockingly needling totter endlessly

indicators.note: without an end means the last letter is cut off
a needle pierces into something, so one piece pushes inside the other

parts.note: REEL, to totter, minus its last letter
cit is an old contemptuous word for a townsman

explanation.surface: A city slicker is teased while someone staggers about.
explanation.walkthrough: Cit was the scornful word aristocrats used for a tradesman of the City, hence 'mockingly'.
explanation.definitionFit: To recite is to enumerate or narrate the particulars of something, which is giving details of it.

clue.text: Those appearing to pray otherwise meant end of this

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so the letters take another order

parts.note: the five letters rearranged

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

parts.note: the last letter of this

explanation.surface: Worshippers who only look devout meant something else entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: MANTES is a plural of mantis, the insect that holds its forelegs as if in prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Praying mantises fold their front legs as if in prayer, so they only look as though they pray.

clue.text: Unusually normal hostel where handouts were once available

indicators.note: unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters take an unusual order

parts.note: the six letters rearranged
the Y is short for a YMCA or YWCA hostel

explanation.surface: An odd, ordinary lodging that used to give out charity.
explanation.definitionFit: An almonry was the place, often at a monastery, where alms were distributed to the poor.

clue.text: Guys keeping up are those with stamina?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: things that stay or prop something up, as guy ropes do
second meaning: horses or runners able to last a long distance

explanation.surface: Men who keep pace must be the ones with endurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guys' suggests men keeping pace; here they are guy ropes, which stay a structure.
explanation.definitionFit: A stayer is literally one that stays or supports, and also a racehorse or athlete with endurance.

clue.text: Fret about restricting a plant which emits a stink

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word is read backwards
to restrict is to hem in, so the word encloses a letter

parts.note: to fret is to worry
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone frets over a foul-smelling weed hemming them in.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal happens first; the A then goes in after the first letter of the turned word.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarrow, or milfoil, is a strong-scented herb, so a plant known for its pungent smell.

clue.text: Women vindicate Scots chippy

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
to right a wrong is to vindicate

explanation.surface: Women defend a touchy Scotsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chippy' suggests touchy, but it is British slang for a carpenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Wright survives in Scotland as the ordinary word for a carpenter or joiner, which a chippy is.

clue.text: Mostly high-pitched answer upset consort

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
upset means turned over, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: TREBLE, high-pitched, without its last letter
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A shrill reply annoys a royal spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: TREBL + A reversed gives the answer; Prince Albert was Queen Victoria's husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert was the Prince Consort, the husband of Queen Victoria, so the archetypal royal consort.

clue.text: Joined anonymous escort around noon

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for anonymous

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one word wraps the letter

parts.note: a date is a companion on an outing
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: An unnamed companion met up at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: A + DA(N)TE.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany, adnate describes organs grown together or attached along their length, so joined.

clue.text: What identifies Jeanne, eg, and minor attendant

parts.note: Ste, Sainte, is the French title before a female saint such as Jeanne d'Arc
a ward is a minor under a guardian's care

explanation.surface: A French girl's name tag and a young helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jeanne, eg' points to a French female saint, whose title is abbreviated Ste.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward serves passengers or guests, so an attendant in the broad sense.

clue.text: Sharp son discarded option

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
a wish is a choice one would have made, set aside

explanation.surface: A keen young man throws away his chance.
explanation.definitionFit: Swish and sharp are both informal adjectives for smart and stylish, as in a sharp suit.

clue.text: Former naval staff take in teeming metropolises

indicators.note: in places one letter within the word

parts.note: a wen is a large congested city, as Cobbett's great wen, London
R stands for recipe, Latin take, on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Ex-navy personnel are drafted into crowded capitals.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside WENS. The Wrens were the Women's Royal Naval Service, absorbed into the Royal Navy in 1993.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrens were members of the Women's Royal Naval Service, a branch that no longer exists separately.

clue.text: This is spent by Chinese, one with a duck

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for Chinese
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A man in China pays for a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chinese' reads as part of the definition, telling you whose money it is, as well as giving its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The chiao, or jiao, is a Chinese monetary unit worth a tenth of a yuan, so money that gets spent.

clue.text: Cross about each fag

indicators.note: about here means around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: wry means cross or perverse
EA is the abbreviation for each

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed about each cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fag' is the British verb meaning to tire, not a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: To fag is British for to tire out, and to weary means the same.

clue.text: Yahoo earlier on to stop flipping cheer of expectant delight

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the combined letters are read back to front

parts.note: a yahoo is a lout, a yob
ho is an old call or word meaning a stop

explanation.surface: A lout shouts with delight before a mad, flipping halt.
explanation.walkthrough: YOB comes first, then HO; the whole is reversed to read OH BOY.
explanation.definitionFit: Oh boy is the exclamation people give when they eagerly anticipate something good.

clue.text: Inspiration is smart in love

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: agape is the Greek word for selfless Christian love
to smart or sting is to nip

explanation.surface: Being in love gives a stinging, clever spark of creativity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' looks like clever, but it is the verb meaning to sting.
explanation.definitionFit: Aganippe was the spring on Mount Helicon sacred to the Muses, its waters a source of poetic inspiration.

clue.text: Carp about old credit? Au contraire — there'll be no stink over it

definitions.text: there'll be no stink over it

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other
French for on the contrary, it swaps which piece goes outside and which inside

parts.note: strap is old slang for credit, especially for drink
the tench is a fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about an outdated loan, then insists it is no scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the fish goes round the credit; 'Au contraire' reverses that, so the credit holds the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A stench trap is the water seal in a drain that stops sewer smells rising, so nothing smells above it.

clue.text: True, his trilling is rough

indicators.note: a trill makes notes quiver and shake, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone admits his singing voice is coarse.
explanation.definitionFit: Hirsute means hairy or shaggy, and rough can describe a coarse, hairy surface.

clue.text: Ending rounds with yen for dash of tequila

indicators.note: putting one thing for another means a swap of letters

parts.note: tours are rounds of visits
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen

indicators.note: a dash is a small amount, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: first letter of tequila

explanation.surface: A night of drinking ends with someone's yen for a splash of spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: In TOURS the Y replaces the T. 'Ending' is the definition: the closing word of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Yours, as in 'Yours sincerely', is the conventional sign-off at the close of a letter.
